messages.content: What is Reagent and how do I create a basic component?

Reagent is a minimalistic ClojureScript interface to React. It lets you build React components using Clojure data structures and functions. **Setup** ```clojure ;; deps.edn {:deps {reagent/reagent {:mvn/version "1.2.0"}}} ;; Require in your namespace (ns myapp.core (:require [reagent.core :as r] [reagent.dom :as rdom])) ``` **Form-1: Simple Function Component** ```clojure ;; Just a function returning Hiccup (defn greeting [name] [:h1 "Hello, " name "!"]) ;; Usage [greeting "World"] ;; Renders:

Hello, World!

``` **Hiccup Syntax** ```clojure ;; Basic: [tag attrs? children...] [:div {:class "container"} [:h1 "Title"] [:p "Paragraph text"]] ;; CSS shortcuts [:div.container] ; class="container" [:div#main] ; id="main" [:div#main.container.active] ; id="main" class="container active" ;; Inline styles [:div {:style {:color "red" :font-size "16px"}}] ;; Event handlers [:button {:on-click #(js/alert "Clicked!")} "Click me"] ``` **Rendering to DOM** ```clojure (defn app [] [:div [:h1 "My App"] [greeting "Reagent"]]) ;; Mount the app (defn ^:export init [] (rdom/render [app] (.getElementById js/document "app"))) ``` **Complete Example** ```clojure (ns myapp.core (:require [reagent.core :as r] [reagent.dom :as rdom])) ;; Components (defn nav-link [href text] [:a.nav-link {:href href} text]) (defn navbar [] [:nav.navbar [nav-link "/" "Home"] [nav-link "/about" "About"] [nav-link "/contact" "Contact"]]) (defn main-content [] [:main [:h1 "Welcome to My App"] [:p "This is built with Reagent and ClojureScript."]]) (defn footer [] [:footer [:p "© 2024 My App"]]) (defn app [] [:div#app-container [navbar] [main-content] [footer]]) ;; Entry point (defn ^:export init [] (rdom/render [app] (.getElementById js/document "root"))) ```
How do I manage local state in Reagent components?

Reagent uses special reactive atoms (`r/atom`) for state management. When a component derefs a ratom, it automatically re-renders when that atom changes.

**Form-2: Components with Local State**
```clojure
;; Returns a FUNCTION that closes over state
(defn counter []
  (let [count (r/atom 0)]  ; Local state
    (fn []  ; Render function
      [:div
        [:p "Count: " @count]
        [:button {:on-click #(swap! count inc)} "+"]
        [:button {:on-click #(swap! count dec)} "-"]])))

;; The outer function runs once (setup)
;; The inner function runs on every render
```

**Important: Form-2 Pattern**
```clojure
;; WRONG - creates new atom on each render
(defn broken-counter []
  (let [count (r/atom 0)]  ; Recreated every render!
    [:div
      [:p "Count: " @count]
      [:button {:on-click #(swap! count inc)} "+"]]))

;; CORRECT - atom created once, inner fn re-runs
(defn working-counter []
  (let [count (r/atom 0)]  ; Created once
    (fn []                  ; This re-runs on render
      [:div
        [:p "Count: " @count]
        [:button {:on-click #(swap! count inc)} "+"]])))
```

**Preserving Props in Form-2**
```clojure
;; When inner function needs props, accept them again
(defn editable-field [initial-value]
  (let [editing? (r/atom false)
        value (r/atom initial-value)]
    (fn [initial-value]  ; Accept props again!
      [:div
        (if @editing?
          [:input {:value @value
                   :on-change #(reset! value (.. % -target -value))
                   :on-blur #(reset! editing? false)}]
          [:span {:on-click #(reset! editing? true)}
            @value])])))
```

**r/atom vs clojure.core/atom**
```clojure
;; r/atom - reactive, triggers re-render
(def app-state (r/atom {:count 0}))

;; Deref in component = subscription
(defn display []
  [:p "Count: " (:count @app-state)])  ; Re-renders on change

;; Regular atom - NOT reactive
(def non-reactive (atom 0))
;; Deref won't trigger re-render!
```

**Practical Examples**
```clojure
;; Toggle visibility
(defn collapsible [title content]
  (let [open? (r/atom false)]
    (fn [title content]
      [:div.collapsible
        [:h3 {:on-click #(swap! open? not)}
          (if @open? "▼ " "▶ ") title]
        (when @open?
          [:div.content content])])))

;; Form with multiple fields
(defn signup-form []
  (let [form-data (r/atom {:name "" :email "" :password ""})]
    (fn []
      [:form {:on-submit (fn [e]
                           (.preventDefault e)
                           (js/console.log @form-data))}
        [:input {:placeholder "Name"
                 :value (:name @form-data)
                 :on-change #(swap! form-data assoc :name (.. % -target -value))}]
        [:input {:type "email"
                 :placeholder "Email"
                 :value (:email @form-data)
                 :on-change #(swap! form-data assoc :email (.. % -target -value))}]
        [:input {:type "password"
                 :placeholder "Password"
                 :value (:password @form-data)
                 :on-change #(swap! form-data assoc :password (.. % -target -value))}]
        [:button {:type "submit"} "Sign Up"]])))

;; Todo list
(defn todo-list []
  (let [todos (r/atom [{:id 1 :text "Learn Reagent" :done? false}
                       {:id 2 :text "Build an app" :done? false}])
        next-id (r/atom 3)
        new-todo (r/atom "")]
    (fn []
      [:div.todo-list
        [:h2 "Todo List"]
        [:ul
          (for [{:keys [id text done?]} @todos]
            ^{:key id}
            [:li {:class (when done? "completed")}
              [:input {:type "checkbox"
                       :checked done?
                       :on-change #(swap! todos
                                     (fn [t] (map (fn [item]
                                                    (if (= (:id item) id)
                                                      (update item :done? not)
                                                      item)) t)))}]
              text])]
        [:input {:value @new-todo
                 :on-change #(reset! new-todo (.. % -target -value))
                 :placeholder "New todo..."}]
        [:button {:on-click (fn []
                              (when (seq @new-todo)
                                (swap! todos conj {:id @next-id
                                                   :text @new-todo
                                                   :done? false})
                                (swap! next-id inc)
                                (reset! new-todo "")))}
          "Add"]])))
```
How do I create Reagent components with lifecycle methods?

Form-3 components give you access to React lifecycle methods using `r/create-class`.

**Form-3: Full Lifecycle Control**
```clojure
(defn canvas-component []
  (r/create-class
    {:display-name "canvas-component"
     
     ;; Lifecycle methods
     :component-did-mount
     (fn [this]
       (let [canvas (rdom/dom-node this)
             ctx (.getContext canvas "2d")]
         (.fillRect ctx 0 0 100 100)))
     
     :component-did-update
     (fn [this old-argv]
       (println "Component updated"))
     
     :component-will-unmount
     (fn [this]
       (println "Component unmounting, cleanup here"))
     
     ;; Render function (required)
     :reagent-render
     (fn []
       [:canvas {:width 200 :height 200}])}))
```

**Available Lifecycle Methods**
```clojure
(r/create-class
  {:display-name "my-component"
   
   ;; Mounting
   :constructor
   (fn [this props])
   
   :component-will-mount           ; Deprecated in React 17+
   (fn [this])
   
   :component-did-mount
   (fn [this]
     ;; DOM is available, good for:
     ;; - D3 initialization
     ;; - Third-party library setup
     ;; - Fetching data
     ;; - Setting up subscriptions
     )
   
   ;; Updating
   :should-component-update
   (fn [this old-argv new-argv]
     ;; Return false to prevent re-render
     true)
   
   :component-will-receive-props    ; Deprecated
   (fn [this new-argv])
   
   :component-will-update           ; Deprecated
   (fn [this new-argv])
   
   :component-did-update
   (fn [this old-argv]
     ;; Runs after re-render
     ;; Good for DOM manipulation after update
     )
   
   ;; Unmounting
   :component-will-unmount
   (fn [this]
     ;; Cleanup:
     ;; - Remove event listeners
     ;; - Cancel timers
     ;; - Close connections
     )
   
   ;; Error handling
   :component-did-catch
   (fn [this error info]
     ;; Handle errors in children
     )
   
   ;; Required
   :reagent-render
   (fn []
     [:div "Hello"])})
```

**Accessing Props and State**
```clojure
(defn my-component [name]
  (r/create-class
    {:component-did-mount
     (fn [this]
       ;; Access current props
       (let [[_ name] (r/argv this)]  ; First element is component
         (println "Mounted with name:" name)))
     
     :component-did-update
     (fn [this old-argv]
       (let [[_ old-name] old-argv
             [_ new-name] (r/argv this)]
         (when (not= old-name new-name)
           (println "Name changed from" old-name "to" new-name))))
     
     :reagent-render
     (fn [name]  ; Props available directly
       [:div "Hello, " name])}))
```

**Practical Examples**
```clojure
;; Timer component
(defn timer []
  (let [seconds (r/atom 0)
        interval-id (atom nil)]
    (r/create-class
      {:component-did-mount
       (fn [this]
         (reset! interval-id
           (js/setInterval #(swap! seconds inc) 1000)))
       
       :component-will-unmount
       (fn [this]
         (js/clearInterval @interval-id))
       
       :reagent-render
       (fn []
         [:div "Elapsed: " @seconds " seconds"])})))

;; Third-party library integration (e.g., Chart.js)
(defn chart [data]
  (let [chart-instance (atom nil)]
    (r/create-class
      {:component-did-mount
       (fn [this]
         (let [canvas (rdom/dom-node this)
               ctx (.getContext canvas "2d")]
           (reset! chart-instance
             (js/Chart. ctx (clj->js {:type "bar"
                                      :data data})))))
       
       :component-did-update
       (fn [this old-argv]
         (let [[_ new-data] (r/argv this)]
           (set! (.-data @chart-instance) (clj->js new-data))
           (.update @chart-instance)))
       
       :component-will-unmount
       (fn [this]
         (.destroy @chart-instance))
       
       :reagent-render
       (fn [data]
         [:canvas {:width 400 :height 300}])})))

;; Focus input on mount
(defn auto-focus-input []
  (r/create-class
    {:component-did-mount
     (fn [this]
       (.focus (rdom/dom-node this)))
     
     :reagent-render
     (fn []
       [:input {:placeholder "I'll be focused!"}])}))
```

**Using with-let for Simpler Cleanup**
```clojure
;; Reagent's with-let handles cleanup automatically
(defn timer-simple []
  (r/with-let [seconds (r/atom 0)
               interval-id (js/setInterval #(swap! seconds inc) 1000)]
    [:div "Elapsed: " @seconds " seconds"]
    ;; finally clause runs on unmount
    (finally
      (js/clearInterval interval-id))))
```
How do I handle forms and user input in Reagent?

Reagent makes form handling straightforward with controlled components and ratoms.

**Basic Input Binding**
```clojure
(defn simple-input []
  (let [value (r/atom "")]
    (fn []
      [:div
        [:input {:value @value
                 :on-change #(reset! value (.. % -target -value))}]
        [:p "You typed: " @value]])))
```

**Form with Multiple Fields**
```clojure
(defn contact-form []
  (let [form (r/atom {:name ""
                      :email ""
                      :message ""})]
    (fn []
      [:form {:on-submit (fn [e]
                           (.preventDefault e)
                           (println "Submitting:" @form)
                           (reset! form {:name "" :email "" :message ""}))}
        [:div.form-group
          [:label "Name"]
          [:input {:value (:name @form)
                   :on-change #(swap! form assoc :name (.. % -target -value))}]]
        
        [:div.form-group
          [:label "Email"]
          [:input {:type "email"
                   :value (:email @form)
                   :on-change #(swap! form assoc :email (.. % -target -value))}]]
        
        [:div.form-group
          [:label "Message"]
          [:textarea {:value (:message @form)
                      :on-change #(swap! form assoc :message (.. % -target -value))}]]
        
        [:button {:type "submit"} "Send"]])))
```

**Reusable Input Component**
```clojure
(defn input-field [{:keys [label type value on-change placeholder]}]
  [:div.form-group
    (when label [:label label])
    [:input {:type (or type "text")
             :value @value
             :placeholder placeholder
             :on-change #(reset! value (.. % -target -value))}]])

;; Usage
(defn my-form []
  (let [name (r/atom "")
        email (r/atom "")]
    (fn []
      [:form
        [input-field {:label "Name" :value name}]
        [input-field {:label "Email" :type "email" :value email}]
        [:button "Submit"]])))
```

**Different Input Types**
```clojure
(defn all-input-types []
  (let [text (r/atom "")
        number (r/atom 0)
        checked (r/atom false)
        selected (r/atom "option1")
        multi-select (r/atom #{})]
    (fn []
      [:form
        ;; Text
        [:input {:type "text"
                 :value @text
                 :on-change #(reset! text (.. % -target -value))}]
        
        ;; Number
        [:input {:type "number"
                 :value @number
                 :on-change #(reset! number (js/parseInt (.. % -target -value)))}]
        
        ;; Checkbox
        [:label
          [:input {:type "checkbox"
                   :checked @checked
                   :on-change #(swap! checked not)}]
          "I agree"]
        
        ;; Radio buttons
        [:div
          (for [option ["option1" "option2" "option3"]]
            ^{:key option}
            [:label
              [:input {:type "radio"
                       :name "my-radio"
                       :value option
                       :checked (= @selected option)
                       :on-change #(reset! selected (.. % -target -value))}]
              option])]
        
        ;; Select dropdown
        [:select {:value @selected
                  :on-change #(reset! selected (.. % -target -value))}
          [:option {:value "option1"} "Option 1"]
          [:option {:value "option2"} "Option 2"]
          [:option {:value "option3"} "Option 3"]]
        
        ;; Multi-select with checkboxes
        [:div
          (for [option ["a" "b" "c"]]
            ^{:key option}
            [:label
              [:input {:type "checkbox"
                       :checked (contains? @multi-select option)
                       :on-change #(swap! multi-select
                                     (if (contains? @multi-select option)
                                       disj
                                       conj)
                                     option)}]
              option])]])))
```

**Form Validation**
```clojure
(defn validated-form []
  (let [form (r/atom {:email "" :password ""})
        errors (r/atom {})
        
        validate (fn []
          (reset! errors {})
          (when (empty? (:email @form))
            (swap! errors assoc :email "Email is required"))
          (when (not (re-matches #".+@.+\..+" (:email @form)))
            (swap! errors assoc :email "Invalid email format"))
          (when (< (count (:password @form)) 8)
            (swap! errors assoc :password "Password must be at least 8 characters"))
          (empty? @errors))
        
        handle-submit (fn [e]
          (.preventDefault e)
          (when (validate)
            (println "Form is valid, submitting...")))]
    (fn []
      [:form {:on-submit handle-submit}
        [:div.form-group
          [:label "Email"]
          [:input {:type "email"
                   :class (when (:email @errors) "error")
                   :value (:email @form)
                   :on-change #(swap! form assoc :email (.. % -target -value))}]
          (when-let [error (:email @errors)]
            [:span.error-message error])]
        
        [:div.form-group
          [:label "Password"]
          [:input {:type "password"
                   :class (when (:password @errors) "error")
                   :value (:password @form)
                   :on-change #(swap! form assoc :password (.. % -target -value))}]
          (when-let [error (:password @errors)]
            [:span.error-message error])]
        
        [:button {:type "submit"} "Sign In"]])))
```

**Debounced Input**
```clojure
(defn debounced-input []
  (let [value (r/atom "")
        debounced-value (r/atom "")
        timeout (atom nil)]
    (fn []
      [:div
        [:input {:value @value
                 :on-change (fn [e]
                              (let [v (.. e -target -value)]
                                (reset! value v)
                                (when @timeout
                                  (js/clearTimeout @timeout))
                                (reset! timeout
                                  (js/setTimeout
                                    #(reset! debounced-value v)
                                    300))))}]
        [:p "Immediate: " @value]
        [:p "Debounced: " @debounced-value]])))
```
How do I use cursors in Reagent for focused state updates?

Cursors provide a way to create a reactive view into a subset of a ratom's data. Changes to a cursor update the underlying atom.

**Basic Cursor Usage**
```clojure
(def app-state (r/atom {:user {:name "Alice"
                               :email "alice@example.com"}
                        :settings {:theme "dark"
                                   :notifications true}}))

;; Create a cursor to a nested path
(def user-cursor (r/cursor app-state [:user]))
(def name-cursor (r/cursor app-state [:user :name]))
(def theme-cursor (r/cursor app-state [:settings :theme]))

;; Reading
@user-cursor
;; => {:name "Alice" :email "alice@example.com"}

@name-cursor
;; => "Alice"

;; Writing - updates the root atom
(reset! name-cursor "Bob")
;; app-state is now {:user {:name "Bob" :email "..."} ...}

(swap! user-cursor assoc :phone "555-1234")
;; app-state is now {:user {:name "Bob" :email "..." :phone "555-1234"} ...}
```

**Cursors in Components**
```clojure
;; Component that only re-renders when its specific data changes
(defn user-profile [user-cursor]
  [:div.profile
    [:h2 "Profile"]
    [:p "Name: " (:name @user-cursor)]
    [:p "Email: " (:email @user-cursor)]])

(defn settings-panel [settings-cursor]
  [:div.settings
    [:h2 "Settings"]
    [:label
      [:input {:type "checkbox"
               :checked (:notifications @settings-cursor)
               :on-change #(swap! settings-cursor update :notifications not)}]
      "Enable notifications"]
    [:select {:value (:theme @settings-cursor)
              :on-change #(swap! settings-cursor assoc :theme (.. % -target -value))}
      [:option {:value "light"} "Light"]
      [:option {:value "dark"} "Dark"]]])

(defn app []
  (let [user-cursor (r/cursor app-state [:user])
        settings-cursor (r/cursor app-state [:settings])]
    [:div
      [user-profile user-cursor]
      [settings-panel settings-cursor]]))
```

**Editable Field with Cursor**
```clojure
(defn editable-field [cursor label]
  [:div.field
    [:label label]
    [:input {:value @cursor
             :on-change #(reset! cursor (.. % -target -value))}]])

(defn user-form []
  [:div
    [editable-field (r/cursor app-state [:user :name]) "Name"]
    [editable-field (r/cursor app-state [:user :email]) "Email"]
    [editable-field (r/cursor app-state [:user :phone]) "Phone"]])
```

**Computed Cursors (Custom Getters/Setters)**
```clojure
;; Create a cursor with custom transformation
(defn computed-cursor [source-atom get-fn set-fn]
  (r/cursor source-atom
    (fn [data]
      (get-fn data))
    (fn [data new-val]
      (set-fn data new-val))))

;; Example: cursor that uppercases
(def uppercase-name
  (computed-cursor app-state
    (fn [data] (-> data :user :name str/upper-case))
    (fn [data new-val] (assoc-in data [:user :name] new-val))))
```

**Cursors vs Direct Deref**
```clojure
;; Without cursor - component re-renders on ANY app-state change
(defn inefficient-component []
  [:div
    [:p "Name: " (:name (:user @app-state))]])  ; Deref entire atom

;; With cursor - only re-renders when user.name changes
(defn efficient-component []
  (let [name-cursor (r/cursor app-state [:user :name])]
    (fn []
      [:div
        [:p "Name: " @name-cursor]])))  ; Focused deref
```

**Cursor Pattern for Lists**
```clojure
(def items-state (r/atom {:items [{:id 1 :name "Item 1" :done false}
                                  {:id 2 :name "Item 2" :done false}]}))

(defn item-component [item-cursor]
  [:li
    [:input {:type "checkbox"
             :checked (:done @item-cursor)
             :on-change #(swap! item-cursor update :done not)}]
    (:name @item-cursor)])

(defn items-list []
  (let [items (r/cursor items-state [:items])]
    [:ul
      (for [i (range (count @items))]
        ^{:key i}
        [item-component (r/cursor items-state [:items i])])]))
```

**r/track for Computed Values**
```clojure
;; r/track creates a reactive computed value (read-only)
(def user-name (r/cursor app-state [:user :name]))
(def user-email (r/cursor app-state [:user :email]))

;; Computed value that reacts to its dependencies
(def user-display
  (r/track
    (fn []
      (str @user-name " <" @user-email ">"))))

(defn display-component []
  [:div
    [:p "User: " @user-display]])  ; Re-renders when name OR email changes
```
What are keys in Reagent and why are they important for lists?

Keys help React identify which items have changed, been added, or removed in lists. They're essential for performance and correctness.

**Why Keys Matter**
```clojure
;; Without keys - React can't efficiently track items
(defn bad-list [items]
  [:ul
    (for [item items]
      [:li (:name item)])])  ; Warning: Each child should have a unique key

;; With keys - React can track items efficiently
(defn good-list [items]
  [:ul
    (for [item items]
      ^{:key (:id item)}  ; Metadata key
      [:li (:name item)])])
```

**Key Syntax Options**
```clojure
;; Metadata syntax (preferred)
^{:key id}
[:li "Item"]

;; In element attributes
[:li {:key id} "Item"]

;; Short metadata syntax
^{:key id} [:li "Item"]
```

**What to Use as Keys**
```clojure
;; GOOD: Stable, unique IDs from your data
(for [user users]
  ^{:key (:id user)}
  [user-card user])

;; GOOD: Unique business identifier
(for [product products]
  ^{:key (:sku product)}
  [product-card product])

;; OKAY for static lists: Index (but avoid for dynamic lists)
(for [[idx item] (map-indexed vector static-items)]
  ^{:key idx}
  [:li item])

;; BAD: Random keys (defeats the purpose)
(for [item items]
  ^{:key (random-uuid)}  ; Don't do this!
  [:li item])
```

**Problems Without Proper Keys**
```clojure
;; Example: Input state gets mixed up
(defn problem-demo []
  (let [items (r/atom [{:id 1 :text "First"}
                       {:id 2 :text "Second"}
                       {:id 3 :text "Third"}])]
    (fn []
      [:div
        [:button {:on-click #(swap! items (fn [xs] (vec (reverse xs))))}
          "Reverse"]
        ;; Without keys: inputs will have wrong values after reverse!
        [:ul
          (for [item @items]
            [:li
              [:input {:default-value (:text item)}]  ; Uses default-value
              (:text item)])]])))

;; Fixed with keys
(defn fixed-demo []
  (let [items (r/atom [{:id 1 :text "First"}
                       {:id 2 :text "Second"}
                       {:id 3 :text "Third"}])]
    (fn []
      [:div
        [:button {:on-click #(swap! items (fn [xs] (vec (reverse xs))))}
          "Reverse"]
        [:ul
          (for [item @items]
            ^{:key (:id item)}  ; Now inputs track correctly
            [:li
              [:input {:default-value (:text item)}]
              (:text item)])]])))
```

**Keys with map and mapv**
```clojure
;; Using map - must return sequence of keyed elements
(defn users-list [users]
  [:ul
    (map (fn [user]
           ^{:key (:id user)}
           [:li (:name user)])
         users)])

;; Alternative: map-indexed when you have no IDs
(defn simple-list [items]
  [:ul
    (map-indexed
      (fn [idx item]
        ^{:key idx}
        [:li item])
      items)])
```

**Keys with Component Children**
```clojure
(defn user-card [user]
  [:div.card
    [:h3 (:name user)]
    [:p (:email user)]])

(defn users-grid [users]
  [:div.grid
    (for [user users]
      ^{:key (:id user)}
      [user-card user])])  ; Key goes on the component usage
```

**Nested Lists and Keys**
```clojure
(defn category-list [categories]
  [:div
    (for [category categories]
      ^{:key (:id category)}
      [:div.category
        [:h2 (:name category)]
        [:ul
          (for [item (:items category)]
            ^{:key (:id item)}  ; Inner list needs its own keys
            [:li (:name item)])]])])
```

**Debugging Key Issues**
```clojure
;; React will warn in console:
;; "Warning: Each child in a list should have a unique 'key' prop."

;; To debug, check:
;; 1. Every item in for/map has a key
;; 2. Keys are unique among siblings
;; 3. Keys are stable (don't change between renders)

(defn debug-list [items]
  [:ul
    (for [item items]
      (do
        (js/console.log "Rendering item with key:" (:id item))
        ^{:key (:id item)}
        [:li (:name item)]))])
```
